## GET /admin-api/tls

`getTlsSettings`

**The TLS certificate's own settings**

The `tls.*` settings: the hostnames and IP addresses that go into the self-signed certificate this service mints on every start, and what it makes of a CLIENT's.

THE CERTIFICATE ONES ARE RESTART-ONLY: it is minted before anything is listening. One certificate serves LDAPS 636 and — when `global.https` is on — the main port, so a caller trusts this service once rather than twice.

THERE ARE NO PORTS HERE SINCE 2026-09-16, when `tls.port` (8443) and `tls.mutualPort` (9443) were removed with the two listeners they named: the main port already asks every connection for a client certificate and requires none of any of them.

Whether the MAIN port is HTTPS is `global.https`, which is on `GET /config` with the rest of the process's own settings: it is a fact about the process rather than about this certificate, and it defaults to whatever `oauth2.rfc9700` is.

THERE IS NO POST BESIDE THIS ONE and that is not a gap: every form on the console page this mirrors posts `set-many` to /admin/config, so `POST /admin-api/config/set-many` is already the operation for it. One store, one action, two doors.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/tls` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## GET /admin-api/tls-connection

`getTlsConnection`

**What this service saw of THIS request: its TLS connection, its client certificate and its forwarding headers**

Describes the request that asked — and only that one — as this service saw and believed it. `connection`: `https`, `encrypted`, the TLS `protocol` and `cipher` negotiated, the socket's `peerAddress` and the `clientAddress` this service believes. `clientCertificate`: whether one was `presented` on the connection, whether it `verified` against the client truststore (`GET /admin-api/tls/trust`) or the `authorizationError` OpenSSL gave, the `certificate` (subject, issuer, serial, validity, subjectAltName, key, SHA-256 fingerprint and PEM), its RFC 8705 `thumbprint`, what the identity gate made of it (`identity`: issued here, accepted, kind, username, realm, why not) and the `revocation` verdict `GET /tls/sign-in` would act on. `forwarded`: `global.trustProxy` and `global.trustedProxies`, whether the peer is a trusted proxy and whether the forwarding headers were `believed`, the `effectiveBaseUrl` every issuer and endpoint is built from, each forwarding header with its value, and the client-certificate headers a proxy might set — which this service READS NONE OF, in either mode.

**IT CHANGES NOTHING**: no session is started (that is `GET /tls/sign-in`), no sighting recorded, no setting written.

**THE CONSOLE'S PAGE DESCRIBES ITS OWN CALL TO THIS OPERATION**, not the request that loaded the page: the console is a static application, so the view is a second request, on whatever connection the browser chose for it. Answered by the front process, which holds the client's socket. Development only as `GET /tls` and `GET /tls/forwarded` until #597.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/tls-connection` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

## GET /admin-api/tls/trust

`getTruststore`

**Every client-certificate trust anchor, and where each came from**

The anchors LDAPS 636 and the main HTTPS port verify a CLIENT certificate against. A certificate that chains to one of these is verified, and a verified certificate is an identity here — it starts a sign-on session and it is what admits a remote XACML PEP to `/xacml/pep/*` — so this list is whose certificates this service believes.

Each row carries the subject, issuer, serial, validity, SHA-256 fingerprint (the colon form `openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256` prints), whether it is a CA, the PEM, and `source`: `file` for one read from `tls.trustAnchorsFile` at startup, `runtime` for one added while the process was running, with `persisted` saying whether it was written down.

**A RUNTIME ANCHOR IS PERSISTED** in `ou=trustAnchors` in the default realm's directory, so it survives a restart wherever the directory does (`persistence.mode` ldif or postgres) and reaches every other process against the same store. A `file` anchor is not stored there and comes back at the next start however it was removed.

**ONE TRUSTSTORE FOR THE PROCESS, NOT PER REALM.** The sockets that verify a client certificate are shared by every trust realm, so this answers the same list under every realm prefix.

**NO PRIVATE KEY IS IN THIS REPLY** — the truststore holds certificates and nothing else.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/tls/trust` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | query | integer |  | Which page of the match to return. CLAMPED rather than refused: a page past the end returns the last one, and the reply says which page it actually is. |
| `per` | query | integer |  | Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 300. On a drill-down it is SHARED by every list in the reply, which each carry a page number of their own. |
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**200**: The anchors on this page with their paging, the counts by source, the configured anchors file, and which doors can change the list.

## POST /admin-api/tls/trust/add

`addTrustAnchors`

**Trust client certificates issued by one or more CAs**

Adds every `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` block in `certificates` — the root, or the whole chain above the leaf — and applies the new truststore to every listener with `setSecureContext()`. The next handshake is judged against it; connections already open keep the truststore they were made under.

**ALL OR NOTHING ON A BLOCK OPENSSL CANNOT READ.** If any block does not parse, none is added: an anchor the listener cannot parse makes the next truststore change throw on every listener. A certificate already held is counted in `duplicates` and not added twice. The truststore holds at most 32 anchors; an add that fills it keeps what went in and says why the rest did not in `warning`.

**PERSISTED** in `ou=trustAnchors` wherever the directory is; `persisted` in the reply says whether every anchor this call added was written down.

**THIS IS THE ONE WAY TO ADD AN ANCHOR AT RUNTIME**, beside the console page that mirrors it, in both modes: the open `POST /tls/trust` was deleted. The reply names what was added and carries no private key, because none is involved.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/tls/trust` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `certificates` | string | yes | One or more PEM certificates, concatenated. An array of PEM strings is accepted too. |

**200**: How many anchors were added, how many were already held, the new total, and the subject and fingerprint of each one added.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `added` | number |  |  |
| `addedAnchors` | list |  |  |
| `addedAnchors[].fingerprint256` | string, or null |  |  |
| `addedAnchors[].source` | string, or null |  |  |
| `addedAnchors[].subject` | string, or null |  |  |
| `anchors` | number |  |  |
| `duplicates` | number |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `persisted` | boolean |  |  |
| `warning` | string |  |  |

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## POST /admin-api/tls/trust/remove

`removeTrustAnchor`

**Stop trusting one anchor, named by its fingerprint**

Removes the ONE anchor whose SHA-256 fingerprint is `fingerprint` — colon-separated or plain hex, either case — and applies the smaller truststore to every listener.

**THERE IS NO BULK CLEAR ON THIS API, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** A clear is the one change whose reach is every client certificate every other caller relies on, and the open `POST /tls/trust/clear` that did it was deleted. Remove the rows you mean.

**A `file` ANCHOR MAY BE REMOVED AND COMES BACK AT THE NEXT START**, when `tls.trustAnchorsFile` is read again; the reply says so. A fingerprint this truststore does not hold is refused and removes nothing.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/tls/trust` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DPoP` | header | string |  | RFC 9449: the proof of possession for a DPoP-bound access token, as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` requires. |
| `cell` | query | string |  | The cell to answer this request, where this service runs as several. Ignored in a service that runs as one. |

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fingerprint` | string | yes | The anchor's SHA-256 fingerprint, as `GET /admin-api/tls/trust` lists it in `fingerprint256`. |

**200**: The anchor that was removed, where it came from, and the new total.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anchors` | number |  |  |

| `ok` | boolean | yes |  |
| `persisted` | boolean |  |  |
| `removed` | number |  |  |
| `removedAnchor` | object |  |  |
